enumeration_rule.rendered_layer: Starting from tutorStubFirstDraftContractPrompt, enumerate every fixed string that can flow into a rendered field downstream of a gate decision from the SHA-pinned services/tutorStubFirstDraftContract.js: every compact uptake branch and rendered opening branch; every COMPACT_PART_CUES value plus the inline scene-partner branch and other compact-part literals; every TACTIC_EXECUTION_CUES value plus compact tactic/support branches and source-accessibility compensation; every compact stance cue; every compact handoff branch; and every compact action cue. Sweep every stance and action-family key mechanically without reachability pruning; exclude constant framing lines that do not vary with a gate decision.
enumeration_rule.templates: For a compact template, quote every fixed segment byte-for-byte in source order and show each interpolated public-contract value as a named {{slot}}; the descriptive prefix states that the gate fills those slots from the public contract, and the drift guard compares the fixed_segments array byte-for-byte.
enumeration_rule.question_support: Do not include buildTutorStubQuestionSupport tutorInstruction strings: they populate the detailed contract ending.instruction field, but the live compact host-plan renderer does not read that field. Include the compact handoff strings selected from question-support state flags instead.

menu_text:
When no narrower uptake branch applies, the compact uptake string is:
<verbatim>
Answer, credit, qualify, correct, or receive the learner’s concrete move; never use generic praise.
</verbatim>

When the public contract records learner acceleration, the compact uptake addition is:
<verbatim>
Credit every warranted move; do not ask for it again.
</verbatim>

When the public contract carries a learner move, this compact uptake template is rendered and the gate fills its named slot from the public contract:
<verbatim>
Carry forward this move: {{learner_move}}
</verbatim>

When a writable entry must precede complementary due evidence, the compact uptake string is:
<verbatim>
Begin exactly “Write:” with one learner-sayable pre-turn limit; do not preview or paraphrase SOURCE.
</verbatim>

When the public contract carries a causal subject and outcome, this compact uptake template is rendered and the gate fills its named slots from the public contract:
<verbatim>
Begin exactly “Write:” with this learner-sayable sentence: “The {{causal_subject}} did not cause the {{causal_outcome}}.” Keep both named roles exact; never widen either role or change cause into prevention.
</verbatim>

When the public contract carries a causal relation without a named subject, the compact uptake string is:
<verbatim>
Begin exactly “Write:” with one learner-sayable sentence: the candidate was inactive while the outcome still occurred, so this rules out candidate causation. Preserve named actors and polarity; never say the candidate failed to prevent or stop the outcome.
</verbatim>

When a writable entry can point to a rendered public record, the compact uptake string is:
<verbatim>
Begin exactly “Write:” with one learner-sayable sentence saying what one numbered RECORD line says. Preserve its actors, relation, and polarity; never reverse cause or evidentiary force, and claim nothing the line does not carry.
</verbatim>

When a writable entry has no rendered public-record block, the compact uptake fallback is:
<verbatim>
Begin exactly “Write:” with one learner-sayable sentence licensed by the public record. Preserve actors, relation, and polarity; never reverse cause or evidentiary force.
</verbatim>

When the public contract requires responsive repair, the compact uptake string is:
<verbatim>
Answer the learner’s unanswered question directly before doing anything else.
</verbatim>

When the public contract selects instructional-meta repair, its rendered opening instruction is:
<verbatim>
Begin by directly acknowledging that the learner wants the explanation made easier to follow. Restate the latest tutor point in ordinary words. Do not quote the whole learner request, treat it as evidence, or advance the inquiry.
</verbatim>

When a writable entry precedes due evidence, its rendered opening instruction is:
<verbatim>
The learner asked what to write while new evidence is due in this reply. Begin exactly with “Write:” and supply one complete learner-sayable sentence about the pre-turn public status or evidentiary limit. It must complement the new evidence: do not state, paraphrase, preview, or summarize any PUBLIC EVIDENCE DUE NOW. Only then enact each due clue once in the development beat.
</verbatim>

When a writable entry is requested without due evidence, its rendered opening instruction is:
<verbatim>
The learner asked what to write. Begin exactly with “Write:” and supply one complete learner-sayable sentence licensed by the current public evidence. This direct entry is the learner uptake; only then perform the selected development beat. Do not substitute a prop action or another question for the requested sentence.
</verbatim>

When no narrower opening branch applies, the rendered opening instruction is:
<verbatim>
Respond to the learner’s actual contribution in the first sentence by answering, crediting, qualifying, correcting, or receiving it. Paraphrase its concrete claim or concern rather than echoing the learner’s substantive wording; do not begin with generic praise.
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the adversarial teacher part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
introduce a subject-native counterexample, altered example, or rival solution at one named lesson object, then require one bounded revision
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the advocate part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
begin “My case is”, state the strongest claim the released public record carries, name what it does not yet establish, and leave the test for HANDOFF
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the authored source part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
enter the public source directly and voice only the supplied evidence
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the exacting schoolmaster part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
require one discipline-specific performance, state its criterion, and permit one precise retry
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the examiner part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
inspect named exhibit; claim no cross-exhibit match absent a public RECORD
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the foreperson part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
gather the public supports, state the licensed finding, and close the record
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the record keeper part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
open, read, mark, enter, or close a public record, separating its entry from what remains unproved
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the satirist part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
catch a polished claim or rote formula contradicting one named public object, expose the mismatch with a wry reversal, and leave a repair path
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the scene partner part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
make room beside one named public object and return its reading to the learner
</verbatim>

When the downstream selector carries the skeptic part, its compact part cue is:
<verbatim>
challenge one unsafe leap and show one fair public route through it
</verbatim>

When the selected part is scene partner, the live inline compact cue is:
<verbatim>
place both speakers at one named public object using “you”, “we”, or “together”; a solitary “I” beside the object does not count; do not ask a question yet
</verbatim>

When no named compact part cue is available, the compact part fallback is:
<verbatim>
perform one concrete public action or judgment
</verbatim>

When the public contract forbids a new prop, the compact part addition is:
<verbatim>
Use an already-named object; add no prop.
</verbatim>

When the public contract permits a scene object, the compact part addition is:
<verbatim>
Name one public scene object.
</verbatim>

For every selected part, this compact wrapper is rendered and the gate fills its named slots from the public contract:
<verbatim>
As {{actorial_part_label}}, without naming the role, {{compact_part_cue}}.
</verbatim>

When the compact tactic builder carries the adversarial pressure tactic, its execution cue is:
<verbatim>
Put direct pressure on the claim rather than the learner and name the public test that could answer it.
</verbatim>

When the compact tactic builder carries the dramatic counterpressure tactic, its execution cue is:
<verbatim>
Make the already-public shortcut or ready judgment identifiable, put contrary public evidence against it through the selected part, and hand the resulting concrete test back to the learner. Perform the collision; do not announce it or rely on a stock verb template.
</verbatim>

When the compact tactic builder carries the dry counterexample tactic, its execution cue is:
<verbatim>
Use the named public object as a dry counterexample, then leave one concrete repair path.
</verbatim>

When the compact tactic builder carries the evidentiary boundary tactic, its execution cue is:
<verbatim>
Name the public evidence, what it supports, and the named conclusion it does not establish. Keep both conclusions explicit; use no pronoun substitute.
</verbatim>

When the compact tactic builder carries the exposed mismatch tactic, its execution cue is:
<verbatim>
Let the named public object expose the mismatch through the action itself rather than explaining the irony.
</verbatim>

When the compact tactic builder carries the measured testimony tactic, its execution cue is:
<verbatim>
Let the public words stand in the character’s voice and explicitly refuse to force a stronger judgment.
</verbatim>

When the compact tactic builder carries the rapid handoff tactic, its execution cue is:
<verbatim>
Move straight from the named public object or line to the learner, ending with the shortest useful concrete question.
</verbatim>

When the compact tactic builder carries the shared scene invitation tactic, its execution cue is:
<verbatim>
Make room beside a named public object for the learner and invite their reading in the same sentence or the next.
</verbatim>

When the compact tactic builder carries the unadorned report tactic, its execution cue is:
<verbatim>
Use one direct first-person action or spoken line in ordinary words; do not add a theatrical preface.
</verbatim>

When support level is three, the compact tactic support string is:
<verbatim>
Make the public connection explicit.
</verbatim>

When support level is two, the compact tactic support string is:
<verbatim>
Give one concrete hint, leaving the judgment open.
</verbatim>

When support level is one, the compact tactic support string is:
<verbatim>
Give only a light directional cue.
</verbatim>

When support level is zero or unset, the compact tactic support string is empty:
<verbatim>

</verbatim>

When source accessibility compensation is active, this compact template is rendered and the gate fills its named slot from the public contract:
<verbatim>
Immediately after SOURCE, write one unquoted statement of at most {{max_words}} words.
</verbatim>

When source accessibility compensation is active, this compact template is rendered and the gate fills its named slot from the public contract:
<verbatim>
Reuse at least {{min_material_source_tokens}} material SOURCE words in order and one source-specific anchor.
</verbatim>

When source accessibility compensation is active, its compact constraint string is:
<verbatim>
Add only a, an, or the; preserve no, not, only, and may; do not copy all SOURCE or ask.
</verbatim>

When public source evidence is active, the compact tactic prefix is:
<verbatim>
After SOURCE closes, make TACTIC a new unquoted sentence.
</verbatim>

When the requested pressure tactic is inapplicable, the compact tactic transition is:
<verbatim>
Use the delivered boundary tactic, not the requested pressure tactic.
</verbatim>

When direction-only support recasts rapid handoff, the compact tactic execution string is:
<verbatim>
Move straight from one already-public object or line to the present evidentiary limit. State the direction of the missing support yourself and end declaratively; do not ask the learner to name unseen evidence.
</verbatim>

When the public contract carries a causal subject and outcome, this tactic template is rendered and the gate fills its named slots from the public contract:
<verbatim>
Say “The {{causal_subject}} did not cause the {{causal_outcome}}; actual cause remains open.” Add no third clause or role change.
</verbatim>

When the handoff owns an allowed question, the compact tactic boundary is:
<verbatim>
Ask no question here; HANDOFF owns it.
</verbatim>

When the public contract forbids a question, the compact tactic boundary is:
<verbatim>
Ask no question here.
</verbatim>

When rapid handoff delegates question ownership, this compact tactic template is rendered and the gate fills its named slot from the public contract:
<verbatim>
Move straight from the named public object or line to one short declarative observation. {{question_boundary}}
</verbatim>

When shared-scene invitation delegates question ownership, this compact tactic template is rendered and the gate fills its named slot from the public contract:
<verbatim>
Invite shared attention to the named public object declaratively using “you”, “we”, or “together”. {{question_boundary}}
</verbatim>

When another tactic delegates question ownership, this compact tactic template is rendered and the gate fills its named slots from the public contract:
<verbatim>
{{tactic_execution}} {{question_boundary}}
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the brisk stance, its compact stance cue is:
<verbatim>
Clip sentences; omit preface, recap, catalogue.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the charismatic stance, its compact stance cue is:
<verbatim>
Stage collision; make a decisive named challenge.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the face threat stance, its compact stance cue is:
<verbatim>
Expose the move locally; leave minimal repair.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the ironic stance, its compact stance cue is:
<verbatim>
Feign concession; let material expose the mismatch.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the plain stance, its compact stance cue is:
<verbatim>
Use literal words; no flourish.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the precise stance, its compact stance cue is:
<verbatim>
Say “X, not Y”; name correction.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the sarcastic stance, its compact stance cue is:
<verbatim>
Mock-praise the claim; reverse it; offer repair.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the warm stance, its compact stance cue is:
<verbatim>
Invite with “we”; preserve genuine choice.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the witnessing stance, its compact stance cue is:
<verbatim>
Reflect concern; lower pressure; leave judgment.
</verbatim>

When the public contract carries an unlisted stance, this compact stance fallback is rendered and the gate fills its named slot from the public contract:
<verbatim>
Make it visibly {{engagement_stance}}.
</verbatim>

When the public contract names a settled surface, the compact handoff addition is:
<verbatim>
Do not reopen the settled point.
</verbatim>

When the public contract requires a sibling-relation bridge, the compact handoff addition is:
<verbatim>
Connect SOURCE to the learner’s requested relation.
</verbatim>

When declarative support has no supplied handoff instruction, the compact handoff fallback is:
<verbatim>
End declaratively; ask no question.
</verbatim>

When questions are forbidden without another special branch, the compact handoff string is:
<verbatim>
State the current public limit through the selected action; ask no question.
</verbatim>

When a handoff question is optional, the compact handoff string is:
<verbatim>
Carry the selected action to TURN FOCUS. HANDOFF may ask one final question there; otherwise end declaratively.
</verbatim>

When active source evidence and stage-next-step require a handoff question, the compact handoff string is:
<verbatim>
Ask one HANDOFF question about what SOURCE changes, supports, or rules out.
</verbatim>

When the default handoff owns the final question, this compact handoff template is rendered and the gate fills its named slot from the public contract:
<verbatim>
{{compact_action_instruction}} HANDOFF owns the one final question.
</verbatim>

When question-support state requires bounded choices, the compact handoff addition is:
<verbatim>
Express two or three recognizable public-safe choices declaratively; do not turn the list into a question.
</verbatim>

When question-support state requires a clarification invitation, the compact handoff addition is:
<verbatim>
Also say that the learner may ask for a direct explanation of one clue, connection, or term.
</verbatim>

When the public contract requires closure, the compact action override is:
<verbatim>
State the licensed public finding and close the inquiry; ask no question.
</verbatim>

When the public contract requires responsive repair, the compact action override is:
<verbatim>
End after the direct answer or one public way to check it; do not substitute another exercise.
</verbatim>

When active source evidence carries stage-next-step, the compact action override is:
<verbatim>
Return SOURCE as one concrete question about what it changes, supports, or rules out.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the answer accountably action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
Name one public way the answer could be checked or corrected.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the baseline plain response action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
End with one compact next move grounded in the public record.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the challenge resistance action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
Offer one small public move that restores choice.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the clarify distinction action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
Ask one concrete test of the distinction just stated.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the clarify term action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
Return one concrete use of the clarified term; do not turn it into a proof test.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the close inquiry action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
State the licensed public finding and close the inquiry; ask no question.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the compress sayback action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
End with the short learner-sayable formulation; do not reopen a settled step.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the ground in material action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
Return the named public object for one concrete judgment.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the reanchor lived stake action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
Return from the scene consequence to the live public evidence.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the reanchor public evidence action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
End on the clue’s current limit, without testing memory.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the receive vulnerability action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
Reduce pressure and leave the next judgment with the learner.
</verbatim>

When the gate carries the stage next step action family, its compact action cue is:
<verbatim>
Name the next available public check; never ask for unseen evidence.
</verbatim>
